Chapter 10: Sustaining Change—Building Habits That Last.
So, you’ve started making changes in your life, and you’re probably wondering, “How do I make these new habits actually stick?” Here’s the thing—lasting change isn’t just about gritting your teeth and powering through. It’s really about building a life, an environment, and relationships that make your new routines feel natural, almost automatic.
Let’s start with making your new habit as easy as possible. Imagine you want to eat healthier. What if, instead of keeping junk food at arm’s reach, you put a bowl of fruit on the counter and prep healthy snacks ahead of time? Or, if you want to work out more, set out your workout clothes the night before. Little tweaks like these remove obstacles, so the behavior you want becomes the path of least resistance.
Another powerful piece of the puzzle? Accountability. Telling someone about your goals, tracking your progress, and celebrating the little wins along the way—these things all help keep you on track. And when setbacks happen—and let’s be honest, they will—having a support system makes it way easier to bounce back and keep moving forward.
Reflection is also key. Every so often, take a step back and ask yourself: “What’s actually working for me? Where am I getting stuck? How can I tweak my routine so it fits my life even better?” This mindset of always learning and improving turns habit change from a one-time thing into a lifelong journey.
Here are some practical steps for making new habits last:
First, design supportive environments—make those good choices easy and accessible.
Second, build accountability—don’t keep your goals to yourself, share them and check in with others.
Third, keep reflecting and adjusting—be open to changing your approach as you learn what works.
And finally, celebrate your progress. Even small milestones deserve recognition—they’ll keep your motivation strong.
In the end, sustaining change is about creating a life that naturally supports your best intentions. When you align your environment, your relationships, and your mindset with your goals, you make it so much easier to keep those positive habits going—and keep growing, day after day.
